problem.explanation: The inner scalar subquery finds the highest salary. The outer MAX chooses the greatest salary below it, which handles duplicate top salaries. A common mistake is OFFSET without considering duplicates. DENSE_RANK is an alternative and generalizes to the nth distinct salary.
hints: Then find the maximum value strictly below that maximum.
problem.reference_solution: SELECT MAX(salary) AS second_highest_salary FROM employees WHERE salary < (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM employees)
problem.statement_markdown: Return the second-highest distinct salary as second_highest_salary. Duplicate top salaries should not change the answer.
problem.title: Second highest salary
